name: Cookies and Tracking Technologies
text: The platform may use cookies and similar tracking technologies to enhance the user experience and collect usage data. Cookies are small data files stored on the user's device. Users may control cookie settings through their browser preferences. The platform uses: (a) essential cookies necessary for the operation of the service; (b) analytics cookies to understand usage patterns; and (c) preference cookies to remember user settings. Users may opt out of non-essential cookies at any time. Processing of data collected through cookies is governed by this Privacy Policy and applicable Indian law.
invalid_if: No opt-out mechanism is provided for non-essential cookies
title: Cookies and Tracking
dispute_hotspots: Implied consent from banner — DPDPA requires specific, informed consent

verification_flags.raised_by: Client review of the NDA and Privacy Policy, September 2026 — 'Review the Section 43A IT Act reference'.
verification_flags.question: Whether section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 is still available to be cited. Section 44(3) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 omits it, but the omission takes effect on the date that provision is brought into force, and the status of the SPDI Rules, 2011 alongside it is not settled between the sources consulted.
verification_flags.why_not_resolved_here: This is a question about what the law currently is, not about how this clause is drafted. It has been recorded on every clause that cites the section rather than answered by editing the citation: eleven clauses across the NDA, employment, IP, privacy and core confidentiality families rest on it, and changing a statutory reference without an advocate would be the system asserting law it cannot verify.
